simple.meaning: נְצִיב (nᵉtsîyb) is a Hebrew word meaning “something stationary , i.e. a prefect , a military post , a statue.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: נְצִיב (H5333) appears 12 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 19:26, with occurrences in Genesis, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, 1 Kings, 1 Chronicles, and 1 more.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נְצִיב (H5333) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in נְצִיב (H5333) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: נְצִיב (nᵉtsîyb) / H5333 is traced through Genesis 19:26, 1 Samuel 10:5, 1 Samuel 13:3, 1 Samuel 13:4 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: something stationary , i.e. a prefect , a military post , a statue
definitions.full: H5333. netsib I. נְצִיב noun masculine pillar, prefect , also apparently garrison, post (Ecclus 46:18 צר נציבי ויבנע and he subdued garrisons, posts, of the foe ); — ׳נ absolute 1Kin 4:19 ; construct 1Sam 13:3 3 t.; plural נְצִיבִים 2Sam 8:6 2 t. + 2Chr 8:10 Kt, נְצִבִים 2Sam 8:14 (twice in verse); construct נְצִבֵי 1Sam 10:5 ᵑ0 , but read ᵑ9 ᵑ6 ᵐ5 נְצִיב Th We Dr Klo Kit Bu HPS; — 1 pillar , ׳נ מֶלַח Gen 19:26 (J). 2 prefect, deputy 1Kin 4:19 (on text compare Klo Benz), so perhaps also 1Sam 10:5 (HPS; pillar ᵐ5 Th Dr Klo Kit), and apparently 13:3-4 , (> al. pillar ); this meaning serves also for 2Sam 8:6 , 14 (twice in verse) (so Ki; Th HPS garrison ) 1Chr 11:16 ; 18:13 ; 2Chr 8:10 (where read Kt), 17:2 (Kau garrison in 11:16 ; 17:2 ; Ecclus 46:18 — see above — would favour this meaning in other passages).
